body.hook: An electrician, a Red Seal chef, a certified dental assistant and a network engineer all have something in common: a credential that tells employers they meet a recognized standard. Knowing which credential your career needs is the first step to getting it.

vocabulary.definition: A qualification that shows you meet a recognized standard.
Official recognition, often by exam, that you meet professional standards.
An interprovincial standard for skilled trades in Canada, letting tradespeople work across provinces.
A credential usually from a college or polytechnic, typically two years.
A credential from a university, typically four years for a bachelor's.
A step-by-step plan to reach a career goal.

study.title: Credential Quest
study.question: What credentials and programs lead to the career I want?
study.passage:
Types of credentials:
• Certificate: short program (months to one year), for example a food safety certificate or a college certificate.
• Industry certification: for example Food Safe, WHMIS, CompTIA A+, Adobe Certified Professional, First Aid.
• Trade certification: apprenticeship + exams leads to journeyperson certification; many trades also offer the Red Seal endorsement.
• Diploma: two-year programs at polytechnics and colleges (for example NAIT and SAIT in Alberta).
• Degree: university bachelor's (usually four years), then master's or professional degrees.
Part 1, Choose (5 minutes): Pick one career connected to your CTS area.
Part 2, Research (25 minutes): Using alis.alberta.ca and post-secondary websites, find: credential required, at least two programs that offer it (name, length, admission requirements, cost), certifications that would help, and whether Red Seal applies.
Part 3, Compare (10 minutes): Compare two pathways to the same career (for example apprenticeship vs diploma).
Part 4, Action plan (10 minutes): Write steps from now to employment: high school courses, certifications to get now, applications, dates.
study.source: Original career research task written for this lesson; credential information summarized from alis.alberta.ca and Red Seal Program sources.
